system_description.narrative_title: Hormuz Deadlock: Iran–U.S. Standoff Disrupts Global Oil
system_description.narrative_summary: An escalating standoff over the Strait of Hormuz—Tehran hardening conditions to reopen the waterway while Washington (Trump) pivots to economic pressure—is the single dominant narrative. As an open system, the crisis links political decisions, military actions, shipping flows, energy markets, and financial expectations through reinforcing and balancing feedbacks (attacks and appointments → shipping disruption and spills → oil-price shocks → market/forecast adjustments → policy shifts). The immediate effects are rising oil prices, disrupted shipping and insurance, shifts in Gulf export routes, and revisions to global supply/demand forecasts.
system_description.scope: Interactions and feedbacks around the Strait of Hormuz crisis during the news window: Iranian political moves and security decisions, U.S. policy responses (economic pressure and military posturing), Gulf states' responses, shipping traffic and attacks, oil production/flows and refinery impacts, commodity and financial market reactions, insurance and rerouting dynamics, and environmental incidents linked to shipping.
system_description.super_system: Global energy–security–economic system (world oil markets, international trade, and geopolitical risk dynamics)
adjacent_subsystems: Persian Gulf regional security and military operations
Global oil production, refining and inventory supply chains
International financial and commodity markets (prices, futures, investor flows)
Maritime shipping, insurance and logistics networks

variables.name: Geopolitical tension level
variables.description: The overall intensity of political and diplomatic confrontation and threat rhetoric between actors influencing the Strait region.

variables.name: Maritime traffic through Hormuz
variables.description: The volume of commercial vessel transits through the Strait per unit time.

variables.name: Oil export volume via Hormuz
variables.description: The quantity of crude and refined oil exported through the Strait of Hormuz per unit time.

variables.name: Alternative routing share
variables.description: The proportion of maritime oil and cargo shipments rerouted away from primary risk-exposed sea lanes.

variables.name: Global oil price
variables.description: The benchmark market price level for crude oil reflecting supply-demand balance and risk premia.

variables.name: Market volatility expectations
variables.description: Market participants' anticipated short- to medium-term volatility for commodities and related financial assets.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium
variables.description: The average insurance cost (premia) charged for vessels and cargo transiting high-risk maritime zones.

variables.name: Refinery throughput rate
variables.description: The rate at which refining capacity is utilized to process crude into refined petroleum products.

variables.name: Global oil inventory
variables.description: Total stocks of crude oil and refined products held in commercial and strategic reserves worldwide.

variables.name: Maritime incident rate
variables.description: The frequency of hostile attacks, collisions, groundings, and oil spills affecting shipping in the region per unit time.

variables.name: Financial risk premium
variables.description: The additional yield or cost of capital demanded by investors to compensate for geopolitical and supply risks.

variables.name: Regional military level
variables.description: The scale and posture of deployed military assets and readiness in and around the maritime chokepoint.

variables.name: Sanctions intensity
variables.description: The breadth and severity of economic restrictions, trade barriers, and financial measures applied in the dispute.

variables.name: Fuel consumption rate
variables.description: The aggregate rate of end-user oil and fuel consumption driving short-run demand.

variables.name: Policy adjustment rate
variables.description: The tempo and magnitude of governmental policy changes (economic, trade, and security) in response to evolving conditions.

variables.name: Environmental damage extent
variables.description: The spatial and ecological extent of pollution and ecosystem harm resulting from oil spills and maritime incidents.

catalysts.title: Iran keeps Strait closed until conditions met
catalysts.description: Iran's declared conditions for reopening the Strait imply continued closure and control, prolonging the transport deadlock and regional tension.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Hormuz Strait to remain closed unless U.S. meets Iran's conditions'; 'Iran says Strait won't open until conditions are met.'

catalysts.title: U.S. shifts to expanded economic pressure/sanctions
catalysts.description: U.S. signaling a renewed economic-pressure campaign against Iran implies stepped-up sanctions and financial measures in coming weeks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump Shifts to Economic Pressure...'; 'Trump says Iran options are let Tehran fail economically or 'hit them really hard.''

catalysts.title: Oman oil slick cleanup and coastal damage
catalysts.description: Large oil slick and salvage operations off Oman will drive ongoing cleanup, environmental harm and local disruption over weeks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Huge oil slick hitting Oman's shoreline'; 'Risk firm Ambrey working to salvage ship spewing oil off Oman.'

catalysts.title: Continuation/expansion of Houthi maritime attacks
catalysts.description: Repeated Houthi strikes in Red Sea and Gulf approaches make further attacks likely, pressuring shipping and security responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthi attack on small cargo ship...'; 'Houthi attack kills six...; US strikes containership.'

catalysts.title: Gulf producers increase non‑Hormuz routing
catalysts.description: States ramp up pipelines and Mediterranean shipments to bypass Hormuz, shifting export routes and trade flows over coming months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi ramps up oil exports through Mediterranean pipeline'; 'Gulf States Accept a New Normal in Hormuz.'

catalysts.title: Further IEA/OPEC revision cycle and market re‑forecasting
catalysts.description: Ongoing downward supply/demand revisions and IEA/OPEC updates will drive market repricing and volatility in coming weeks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'IEA slashes 2026 supply forecast'; 'OPEC Cuts Oil‑Demand Forecast Again as Hormuz Talks Stall.'

catalysts.title: Decision on SPR releases by consumer governments
catalysts.description: Debate over low US SPR levels may produce a release decision or coordinated drawdown to calm markets in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Oil in U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve falls below 300 million barrels,' prompting possible release discussions.
